messages:
mia: Quick heads-up — I'm landing a small migration note in Optimize toolkit about short-sequence batching + quant profiles. Wanted to check: can we surface a tiny Go SDK example in the same page and fix the broken sidebar link to /optimize/batching?

aj: yes please, put the Go snippet under 'Quick examples'. I'll take the sidebar link. Which page is the canonical home for the quant profile table?

mia: currently it's under /optimize/quantization/profiles — but some of the anchors changed after the last doc reorg. That broke cross-links from the quickstart.

docs-bot: @mia created PR #4389 for "optkit: shortseq migration note + examples" — CI started.

sanjay: I can review the quant profile wording. Suggest we add a tiny JSON profile example showing per-layer dtype override for short sequences. Something like:

```json
{
  "profile_name": "shortseq-lowmem",
  "target_dtype": "int8",
  "overrides": {
    "kv_cache_layers": "fp16",
    "attention": "int8"
  },
  "notes": "optimized for seq_len <= 128, improves throughput on T4-equivalent"
}
```

sanjay: also add a one-liner about major regression risk when changing kv_cache_layers.

mia: perfect — I'll paste that. For the Go SDK snippet, can we make it as compact as possible? Something users can copy into a playground quickly.

aj: put this under examples/optkit-quick.go and link from the page. Snippet: 

```go
package main
import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  "github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/redwood"
)
func main(){
  client := redwood.NewClient("$REDWOOD_KEY")
  resp, _ := client.Generate(context.Background(), redwood.Request{Model: "redwood-opt-1", Prompt: "Summarize: ...", MaxTokens: 64})
  fmt.Println(resp.Text)
}
```

eva: tiny UX ask — can the example include a one-line note about enabling batching via the dashboard toggle and the recommended batch_size for shortseq workloads? It's a frequent Q.

mia: added: "recommended batch_size: 8-16 for seq_len <= 128; monitor latency in Console and adjust." I'll push an update to the PR.

aj: sidebar link fixed in a separate commit, pinging docs-bot to re-run checklist.

docs-bot: Checklist: link-check ✅, lint ✅, samples-build ⚠️ (one sample file missing import).

mia: thanks — which import?

docs-bot: the Go sample references "github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/redwood" but the module path in examples repo is "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk" on main.

aj: I'll update the import quickly.

sanjay: quick editorial: change "kv_cache_layers" note to "may need fp16 for stability; verify evals" to avoid sounding prescriptive.

mia: done. Pushed two tiny commits: one swaps the import, one edits the note. CI kicked off.

docs-bot: PR #4389 CI successful — samples built, link-check passed.

eva: lovely. Can someone backfill a short entry in the migration changelog so support can triage questions? A 1-line change log is fine.

mia: adding changelog entry now: "optkit: added short-sequence migration note + small Go/Python examples; fixed sidebar link to batching." Pushed.

aj: I'll merge after a smoke verify on staging site in ~10m.

sanjay: thanks all. If we get support tickets wondering about accuracy drop after quantization, link them to the new profile notes and the eval regression checklist.

mia: noted — I'll add an inline pointer to the eval checklist page before we cut the release."
